title: What pharmacovigilance training does EU GVP Module I require?
description: What EU GVP Module I and Implementing Regulation 520/2012 require for pharmacovigilance training plans, records and QPPV qualification, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: In the EU, Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012 requires every person involved in pharmacovigilance activities at a marketing authorization holder to receive initial and continued training related to their role, and requires training plans and records to be kept and made available for audit or inspection. Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module I adds that training should follow a needs assessment, be checked for effectiveness, and reach staff outside pharmacovigilance whose work can affect it.
keyTakeaways: Article 10(3) of Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012 is the binding training duty for marketing authorization holders; Article 14(2) applies the same duty to national competent authorities and the European Medicines Agency (EMA).

GVP Module I (EMA/541760/2011), legally effective since 2 July 2012, says training plans should be based on a training needs assessment and monitored, with a process to check that training produces the required understanding and conduct.

Training should also be considered for staff without pharmacovigilance tasks whose work may affect the system, such as clinical trials, technical complaints, medical information, sales and marketing, regulatory affairs, legal and audit.

The Qualified Person Responsible for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) must have adequate theoretical and practical knowledge, be assisted by a medically trained person if not medically qualified, and be trained in the MAH's system before taking up the role.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1466 amended 520/2012 from 12 February 2026, but did not change the Article 10 training text. EMA says GVP modules will be updated to reflect the amendments.

regulator: European Commission (Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012); European Medicines Agency (EMA) for GVP guidance; national competent authorities for pharmacovigilance inspections

sections.heading: Where does the EU pharmacovigilance training duty come from?

blocks.text: The training duty is set in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012, and GVP Module I explains how EMA and national inspectors expect it to be met. [Article 10 of Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32012R0520), on management of human resources, requires the marketing authorization holder to have sufficient competent and appropriately qualified and trained personnel for pharmacovigilance activities. Paragraph 3 states:

blocks.title: Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012, Article 10(3)
blocks.text: "All personnel involved in the performance of pharmacovigilance activities shall receive initial and continued training in relation to their role and responsibilities. The marketing authorisation holder shall keep training plans and records for documenting, maintaining and developing the competences of personnel and make them available for audit or inspection."

Article 10(4) adds that the MAH must provide appropriate instructions on processes to be used in case of urgency, including business continuity. [GVP Module I: Pharmacovigilance systems and their quality systems](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-good-pharmacovigilance-practices-module-i-pharmacovigilance-systems-and-their-quality-systems_en.pdf) was adopted on 22 June 2012, and EMA's GVP page lists its legal effective date as 2 July 2012. As at November 2026 it remains the current adopted version, and EMA lists no GVP document under public consultation.

sections.heading: What does GVP Module I expect from a pharmacovigilance training program?

blocks.text: Section I.B.7 of Module I expects needs-based training plans, monitoring, and a check that training changes understanding and conduct. Its main expectations are:

items: **Needs-based plans:** "Training plans should be based on training needs assessment and should be subject to monitoring."

**Purpose:** training should support continuous improvement of skills, the application of scientific progress and professional development, so staff have the qualifications, understanding of pharmacovigilance requirements and experience for their tasks.
**Everyone knows the reporting route:** "All staff members of the organisation should receive and be able to seek information about what to do if they become aware of a safety concern."

**Effectiveness:** there should be a process to check that training results in appropriate understanding and conduct of pharmacovigilance activities, or to identify unmet training needs, in line with organizational and individual development plans.

**Adjacent functions:** adequate training should be considered for staff without assigned pharmacovigilance tasks whose activities may affect the system, including clinical trials, technical product complaints, medical information, terminologies, sales and marketing, regulatory affairs, legal affairs and audits.

blocks.text: Section I.B.6 makes managerial staff responsible for ensuring adequate resources and that training is provided, and section I.B.11 lists training plans and records among the documents of the quality system that must be kept and made available for audit and inspection.

sections.heading: What qualifications and training must the QPPV have?

blocks.text: The QPPV must have adequate theoretical and practical pharmacovigilance knowledge and, if not medically qualified, documented support from a medically trained person. Article 10(1) of the Implementing Regulation requires that where the QPPV has not completed basic medical training under Article 24 of Directive 2005/36/EC, the MAH must ensure the QPPV is assisted by a medically trained person, and that this assistance is duly documented.

Module I section I.C.1.2 expects the MAH to assess the QPPV's qualification before appointment, for example by reviewing university qualifications, knowledge of EU pharmacovigilance requirements and experience. It states that the MAH "should provide the QPPV with training in relation to its pharmacovigilance system, which is appropriate for the role prior to the QPPV taking up the position and which is appropriately documented", with additional training on the products covered where needed. The QPPV must reside and operate in the EU (or, under the EEA agreements, in Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein), per Article 104(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC.

Article 10(2) requires the duties of managerial and supervisory staff, including the QPPV, to be defined in job descriptions, with hierarchy shown in an organizational chart, and the QPPV must have sufficient authority to influence the quality system.

sections.heading: Did the 2025 amendment to the Implementing Regulation change training rules?

blocks.text: No, the training text in Article 10 was not amended, but related obligations changed. [Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1466](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32025R1466) of 22 July 2025 amends Regulation 520/2012 and applies from 12 February 2026.

items: **Subcontracting (new Article 6(3) and (4)):** subcontracts must describe the third party's roles and responsibilities and include audit and inspection arrangements, and third parties may not further subcontract without the MAH's written consent. Training of the third party's staff becomes something the MAH must be able to audit.

**Risk-based audits (amended Article 13(1)):** MAHs must perform risk-based audits of the quality system at regular intervals to confirm compliance with Articles 8, 10, 11 and 12, which includes the Article 10 training requirements, by auditors with no direct involvement in the audited processes.

**Deviations (amended Article 4(3)):** major or critical deviations from pharmacovigilance procedures must be documented in the pharmacovigilance system master file until resolved, which can trigger retraining.

blocks.title: Guidance update pending as at November 2026
blocks.text: EMA's [GVP page](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview/post-authorisation/pharmacovigilance-post-authorisation/good-pharmacovigilance-practices-gvp) states that the amendments made by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1466 are applicable and that GVP will be updated accordingly in upcoming revisions. Until Module I is revised, the 2012 text remains the guidance in force.

blocks.text: Article 12(2) requires pharmacovigilance system elements to be kept for at least five years after the system described in the master file is formally terminated, and product-related pharmacovigilance documents for as long as the product is authorized and at least 10 years after the authorization ends. For record preparation, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) and [how to conduct a training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each pharmacovigilance procedure to the roles that perform or touch it, including adjacent functions such as medical information and sales, and to the assessment points that show understanding. When a procedure changes or a deviation is logged, affected roles can be identified and retrained against the new version. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences) and [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Does EU pharmacovigilance law require annual training?
faqs.a: No fixed interval is set. Article 10(3) of Implementing Regulation 520/2012 requires initial and continued training related to role and responsibilities, and GVP Module I expects needs-based, monitored training plans. MAHs set refresher intervals in their training plans and should be able to justify them during inspection.

faqs.q: Do sales representatives need pharmacovigilance training?
faqs.a: GVP Module I says adequate training should be considered for staff without specific pharmacovigilance tasks whose activities may affect the system, and lists sales and marketing explicitly. In practice sales staff are trained to recognize adverse event information and forward it through the company's reporting route within set timelines.

faqs.q: Must the QPPV be a medical doctor?
faqs.a: No. The QPPV needs adequate theoretical and practical pharmacovigilance knowledge. If the QPPV has not completed basic medical training under Article 24 of Directive 2005/36/EC, the MAH must ensure a medically trained person assists the QPPV and must document that assistance (Article 10(1) of Implementing Regulation 520/2012).

faqs.q: Are training records part of the pharmacovigilance system master file?
faqs.a: Training plans and records are documents of the quality system that must be kept and made available for audit and inspection. GVP Module I lists them among the required quality system documentation. Inspectors commonly request them alongside the master file when assessing the system.
